items.question_text: Your company uses Cloud Storage to store application backup files for disaster recovery purposes. You want to follow Google's recommended practices. Which storage option should you use?
items.solution_text: Google recommends Coldline Storage for disaster recovery because it is designed for data accessed less than once a month with a 90-day minimum storage duration. This class offers the cost-effective balance of durability and availability required for backups that are rarely restored but must be accessible quickly enough to meet recovery time objectives (RTOs), unlike Archive which has high retrieval costs/latency or Standard classes which are over-provisioned for infrequent access.

choices.text: Multi-Regional Storage
Regional Storage
Nearline Storage
Coldline Storage

items.question_text: Several employees at your company have been creating projects with Cloud Platform and paying for it with their personal credit cards, which the company reimburses. The company wants to centralize all these projects under a single, new billing account. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
The goal is to centralize billing, which requires a dedicated corporate billing account.
Creating the account and setting up the payment method in the Google Cloud Platform Console (Option D) is the correct initial step to establish this entity.
Moving projects to an organization (Option C) does not automatically change or create a billing account linkage; individual project-to-billing links must be managed separately.

choices.text: Contact cloud-billing@google.com with your bank account details and request a corporate billing account for your company.
Create a ticket with Google Support and wait for their call to share your credit card details over the phone.
In the Google Platform Console, go to the Resource Manage and move all projects to the root Organizarion.
In the Google Cloud Platform Console, create a new billing account and set up a payment method.

items.question_text: You have an application that looks for its licensing server on the IP 10.0.3.21. You need to deploy the licensing server on Compute Engine. You do not want to change the configuration of the application and want the application to be able to reach the licensing server. What should you do?
items.solution_text: The IP address 10.0.3.21 falls within the RFC 1918 private address range, identifying it as a private/internal IP address rather than a public one. To ensure the application can consistently reach the licensing server at this specific address without configuration changes, you must reserve it as a static internal IP address in GCP Compute Engine. Ephemeral IPs change upon instance restart, and public IP reservations are invalid for private ranges.

choices.text: Reserve the IP 10.0.3.21 as a static internal IP address using gcloud and assign it to the licensing server.
Reserve the IP 10.0.3.21 as a static public IP address using gcloud and assign it to the licensing server.
Use the IP 10.0.3.21 as a custom ephemeral IP address and assign it to the licensing server.
Start the licensing server with an automatic ephemeral IP address, and then promote it to a static internal IP address.

items.question_text: You are deploying an application to App Engine. You want the number of instances to scale based on request rate. You need at least 3 unoccupied instances at all times. Which scaling type should you use?
items.solution_text:
Automatic scaling is the appropriate type because it dynamically adjusts instance counts based on request rate and other metrics as required.
The min_idle_instances parameter specifically ensures a minimum number of unoccupied instances are ready to handle traffic, satisfying the requirement for at least 3 available instances at all times.

choices.text: Manual Scaling with 3 instances.
Basic Scaling with min_instances set to 3.
Basic Scaling with max_instances set to 3.
Automatic Scaling with min_idle_instances set to 3.

items.question_text: You have a development project with appropriate IAM roles defined. You are creating a production project and want to have the same IAM roles on the new project, using the fewest possible steps. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
The gcloud iam roles copy command allows you to duplicate custom IAM roles from one project or organization to another.
Specifying the production project as the destination ensures the roles are copied directly to the target environment with minimal steps, satisfying the requirement for efficiency.
Copying to the organization (Option B) would propagate the roles broadly rather than just to the specific project, while manual creation in the console (Options C and D) is significantly more labor-intensive.

choices.text: Use gcloud iam roles copy and specify the production project as the destination project.
Use gcloud iam roles copy and specify your organization as the destination organization.
In the Google Cloud Platform Console, use the 'create role from role' functionality.
In the Google Cloud Platform Console, use the 'create role' functionality and select all applicable permissions.
